items.title: 69537_Jimmy Jones oral history interview
items.q: We all were depressed about Roosevelt's death, you know, because at that point he was like the father of the country

ctx.x: Can you remember any of the subjects that he talked about?

No, not right off hand. That goes back so far. We were all on 52nd Street, and we were always getting in discussions in between sets, and I think -- this was when Franklin Roosevelt died, the President, you know?

items.title: 69537_Jimmy Jones oral history interview
items.q: I think Roosevelt died in '45 or '46.

ctx.x: And when he died gee whiz, everybody felt bad, you know?
Did Charlie -- you say Charlie was together. In what way did he react to President Roosevelt's death?

Oh, he was let down, you know. But we still had to play our music. And then we were at -- oh, let me -- okay, now this is all coming back to me. We were working at the Onyx Club, still with Stuff Smith, or Ben Webster by this time, because I think Roosevelt died in '45 or '46.
